expected.rationale: A blind tee shot into a fairway that drops away, with Baffling Brook (a stretch of Cobb's Creek) running the left side then wrapping the front, right, and rear of a small, teardrop-shaped green — water guards three sides of the target. Architecture commentary repeatedly calls this 'the ultimate birdie-or-bust hole' where finding the fairway is paramount, a precision/placement test rather than a length test.
sources: Fox News, "US OPEN '13: A hole-by-hole look of Merion Golf Club"
All Golf Holes, 'Merion Golf Club (East Course)'
USGA, 'Looking Back... 1950 U.S. Open at Merion'

approximations: the frequently-quoted Hogan 'hardest tiny par 4' line could not be verified in any source reached and is NOT used as the basis for this expectation; the architecture-writer consensus on the brook/green complex is used instead
the hazard here is Baffling Brook (Cobb's Creek), not Merion's quarry (that belongs to hole 16) — corrected from an earlier mis-hypothesis

the brook wrapping three sides of the green is approximated as two intersecting water-creek segments (front + right), not a continuous water body; the blind tee shot is not modeled (no line-of-sight mechanic)
disagreement: This is a trust failure, not an archetype miss: the observed winner (STRAIGHT) matches the expectation exactly, but the 5-seed winner splits (seed-unstable), so the reading isn't counted as agreement per this harness's trust rule. With a 0.30-stroke margin the average result looks decisive, but a hole with three sides of water around a small green is inherently high-variance (a single mishit can be a full penalty stroke), which plausibly explains why the modal winner isn't unanimous across seeds even when it wins on average. Not connected to the shared STRAIGHT-dominance root cause on augusta-13, since the expected and observed archetypes already agree here.
